findings.claim: Within the observation window the only observed abnormal metric is gateway http_5xx_rate=0.35 ratio at 2026-10-01T12:00:14Z (incident_1001-E-009); topology records show gateway depends on backend, and backend depends on postgres, redis, payment, so gateway sits downstream of backend and cannot be concluded to be the propagation origin from this single symptom alone. findings.claim: A runtime settings configuration change (change_id runtime-1) was applied to backend at 2026-10-01T12:00:10Z; its config diff reduces db_pool_max from 20 to 2 while concurrency=120, a concrete pool-sizing regression observed at the incident's timestamp.

Backend log incident_1001-E-008 observed at 2026-10-01T12:00:14Z carries only the generic excerpt 'Request processing exceeded deadline' and contains no connection-pool acquisition queuing or timeout text, so it neither confirms nor refutes the backend_pool_config_regression mechanism relative to generic resource saturation.

findings.claim: Backend metrics degrade before gateway's observation: backend request_latency_ms=40 ms at 2026-10-01T12:00:00Z and pool_waiters=118 requests at 2026-10-01T12:00:10Z both precede gateway http_5xx_rate=0.35 at 2026-10-01T12:00:14Z, indicating backend-side degradation onset precedes the gateway 5xx symptom rather than following it.
